name: software_deep_engagement

feature_docs.repo_stars_24h: stars the repository received in the 24 complete hours before the star's hour [log1p]
feature_docs.repo_forks_24h: forks of the repository in that window [log1p]
feature_docs.repo_issue_events_24h: issues opened/closed/commented on the repository in that window [log1p]
feature_docs.repo_pr_events_24h: pull requests and reviews on the repository in that window [log1p]
feature_docs.repo_pushes_24h: pushes (commit batches) to the repository in that window [log1p]
feature_docs.repo_events_24h: all public events on the repository in that window [log1p]
feature_docs.repo_org: 1 if the repository is owned by an organisation [raw]
feature_docs.repo_created_in_window: 1 if the repository was created (observed) before the star within the data window [raw]
feature_docs.repo_age_hours: hours since creation when repo_created_in_window, else 0 [log1p]
feature_docs.actor_events_24h: all public events by the developer in the 24 complete hours before the star's hour [log1p]
feature_docs.actor_stars_24h: stars given by the developer in that window [log1p]
feature_docs.actor_forks_24h: forks made by the developer in that window [log1p]
feature_docs.actor_issue_events_24h: issue events by the developer in that window [log1p]
feature_docs.actor_pr_events_24h: pull-request events by the developer in that window [log1p]
feature_docs.actor_pushes_24h: pushes by the developer in that window [log1p]
feature_docs.actor_repo_events_24h: the developer's events on this repository in that window [log1p]
feature_docs.hour_sin: sin(2 pi h / 24), h = UTC hour of the star [raw]

target: deeper engagement (fork, issue or issue comment, pull request or review) by the same developer on the same repository within 24 h of the developer's first star

identification.statement: Associations in public GitHub activity; nothing was randomized.

population: public GitHub accounts and public repositories whose events reached GitHub's public events API and GH Archive between 2024-10-07 and 2024-10-10 UTC (Monday to Thursday); bot accounts excluded from units

selection.rule: lowest validation log loss; confirmed on test by paired bootstrap

limits: Population: public GitHub, 2024-10-07..10 UTC (four weekdays of one autumn week). Developers on GitHub are skewed towards professional, English-speaking and North-American/European/Asian time zones; private repositories and private activity are invisible. GH Archive records the public events API, which drops events under load and omits some activity; counts are lower bounds. Stars are cheap signals inflated by automation and star farming; a star is not evidence of useful adoption (MASTER_SPEC 6.5). These models describe engagement dynamics, not usefulness. Observational associations only: nothing was randomized, so the models do not say what promotion, ranking or buying stars would cause. Short horizon: features look back 24 h and outcomes forward 24 h; long-run adoption, retention, maintenance and dependency incorporation are not observed. Bots are identified only by the '[bot]' login suffix; other automation accounts remain in the data. Deep engagement is measured only as public fork / issue / pull-request events by the same account on the same repository within 24 h of the first star; later engagement, use without public events (cloning, installing, running) and engagement through other accounts are invisible. Stars by repository owners (login equals owner) and by '[bot]' accounts are excluded; only the first star per developer-repository pair in the window is a unit.
extrapolation_limits: Population: public GitHub, 2024-10-07..10 UTC (four weekdays of one autumn week). Developers on GitHub are skewed towards professional, English-speaking and North-American/European/Asian time zones; private repositories and private activity are invisible.
GH Archive records the public events API, which drops events under load and omits some activity; counts are lower bounds.
Stars are cheap signals inflated by automation and star farming; a star is not evidence of useful adoption (MASTER_SPEC 6.5). These models describe engagement dynamics, not usefulness.
Observational associations only: nothing was randomized, so the models do not say what promotion, ranking or buying stars would cause.
Short horizon: features look back 24 h and outcomes forward 24 h; long-run adoption, retention, maintenance and dependency incorporation are not observed.
Bots are identified only by the '[bot]' login suffix; other automation accounts remain in the data.

Deep engagement is measured only as public fork / issue / pull-request events by the same account on the same repository within 24 h of the first star; later engagement, use without public events (cloning, installing, running) and engagement through other accounts are invisible.
Stars by repository owners (login equals owner) and by '[bot]' accounts are excluded; only the first star per developer-repository pair in the window is a unit.

simulator_mapping.unit: a developer (population individual or agent) starring/watching a repository in the software ecosystem for the first time
simulator_mapping.repo_stars_24h: star/watch actions on the repository in the previous 24 simulated hours
simulator_mapping.repo_forks_24h: code.fork calls on the repository in that window
simulator_mapping.repo_issue_events_24h: issue tracker events (issues.create, issues.comment, issues.close) on the repository's project
simulator_mapping.repo_pr_events_24h: pull-request / review events on the repository
simulator_mapping.repo_pushes_24h: code.commit calls (one push per commit batch)
simulator_mapping.repo_events_24h: all of the above plus any other public repository event
simulator_mapping.repo_org: repository owned by an organisation principal
simulator_mapping.repo_created_in_window: repository created by code.create_repo before the star (always observable in the simulator; in the data only creations inside the window were seen)
simulator_mapping.repo_age_hours: simulated hours since creation (the data only covered ages up to about 72 h; cap at 72 when using)
simulator_mapping.actor_*: the same counts for the developer's own actions in the previous 24 simulated hours
simulator_mapping.output: probability that the developer forks, files/comments an issue or opens/reviews a pull request on that repository within 24 simulated hours
simulator_mapping.transform: matrix_from_counts(raw) applies log1p to count features
